text.en: Reducing the Torah to one mitzvah is a matter of concentration, not exemption: great souls could put their whole being into every mitzvah, while small souls must pour themselves into one.

The sequence of generations maps onto the body of Adam HaRishon: the desert generation, who only learned, was the head; the era of the Beis HaMikdash, when tefillah as 'service of the heart' was added, was the heart.
The name 'ikvesa deMeshicha' hints that the last generation is the heel of Adam HaRishon: like the sole of the foot, it has the least feeling and is always in the dark, even under the noon sun.
The very obstacles a person meets in some area are a sign that it is his mission, since the Satan targets precisely what a person was sent to do.
The pervasive loss of faith in today's world is itself the Satan's response to emunah being this generation's mission.

The Rav reads the Chafetz Chaim's prediction that dibbukim would cease as a statement about the test of the generation: a dibbuk revealing people's hidden sins and the soul's suffering would make emunah too easy, and this generation must be tested in emunah.

He reconciles later dibbukim in Eretz Yisrael with the Chafetz Chaim's words by explaining that Hashem's guidance is seen strikingly in Eretz Yisrael anyway, so there the test of emunah is already smaller.

The Rav sees the Satan's hand in the test of each age: in the tzitzis factory whose sales spread unfit tzitzis, and, following the Yaaros Devash, in the custom of black Shabbos clothes that invites brushing off dust on Shabbos.
He contrasts the Torah, where Moshe Rabbeinu boldly foretells the future of the Jewish people, with other religions' books, which do not dare to predict because they would be proven false.
The Rav compares the rare wonders of tzaddikim today to lightning that lights up a dark world for a moment before it is dark again.
The Satan concentrates his attack on whatever mitzvah is a person's main mission, so the very difficulty of emunah today shows that emunah is the mission of this generation.
The intensity of today's assault on emunah is the flare of a dying candle: the Satan knows that Moshiach means his end and is gasping for life.
Following the Tosfos Yom Tov, the Rav compares this generation to the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur: when the Satan concentrates all his force on one target, surviving it is a miracle.
Esav's kiss is itself a bite: the Church's friendliness has done more damage to the Jewish people than its persecutions, and this is the 'vayishakehu with dots' of our time.
The Satan's new power to enter the Jewish home is a condemned prisoner's 'last wish', granted because his end is near.
The chassid's story shows that friends accomplish what neither fear of Gehinnom nor a Rebbe can: shame before his fellow chassidim kept him from sin.
The zarzir is declared like the raven because it keeps company with it: whoever associates with a kind belongs to that family.
Souls in this generation may come from earlier gilgulim, and being exposed to its temptations while remaining Jews is their tikkun.
The placement of Ikvesa d'Meshicha on the 49th and last daf of Sotah matches the 49 days of the Omer, which descend to Malchus she'b'Malchus, the lowest level, just before heaven meets earth.
Unlike past regimes, which persecuted Jews in the name of religion, today's state forbids encouraging belief; the Rav sees this atheism as the Braisa's 'government turned to minus'.
Leaders today are like a dog walking ahead of its master: they seem to be in front but keep looking back to see which way the congregation goes.

The Rav reads the strictness of chametz, nullified by declaring it nothing, as the model for handling thoughts of doubt: the best removal is to treat them as a 'minus quantity' rather than to engage them.
He explains Avraham Avinu throwing dust at the kings as a way of declaring them nothing, the same weapon one uses against doubts.
He reads 'lo sasuru' as a warning not to scout out such thoughts the way the meraglim scouted, trying to explore them and argue against them.

Like the 'be'itah' and 'achishenah' of the general geulah, an individual's trial has a fixed end, but Hashem can shorten it for one who stands firm in emunah, as the exile in Mitzrayim was shortened from 400 to 210 years.

Not waiting for Moshiach shows a lack of belief: a man who knew he would be elected president tomorrow would surely wait for it, so one who truly believed in the promised good would long for Moshiach.
Rabbi Akiva did not truly err about Ben Koziva: he saw in him the soul of Moshiach, and it was the sins of the generation that spoiled it.

The Rambam's Moshiach, who would have every Jew leave his business to follow him and would settle disputes over the place of the mizbeach so that all accept it, is a greater miracle than the wonders the Raavad expects.

The Rav reads the heel as both the generation's weakness and its greatness: it feels nothing and stands in the dark, but the whole body rests on it, so the last generation carries all the generations before it.

Since a test is a promotion, the tenth test should be the hardest; the Rav sharpens this into a question, because the fire of Ur Kasdim, faced for a G-d Avraham had never seen, seems far harder than obeying a G-d who spoke to him.

The difficulty of the Akeidah was not the act but the distance: at Ur Kasdim Avraham jumped into the fire with fervor, while at the Akeidah he went with a heavy heart, holding to emunah when Hashem seemed far.
Avraham could not see an answer that a child learning Rashi knows, because in the time of a nisayon the answer is hidden; the Rav applies this to the questions of his own generation.

Through the Ramban's rule, the Rav makes the Akeidah the pattern of the last exile: just as it was Avraham's last and hardest test, the final generation's test is to hold on to emunah when Hashem seems distant.
The Rav says each generation has its own mitzvah, and the mitzvah of this generation is emunah.
The Rav explains that the Gemara records a date for Moshiach that passed because every date the tzaddikim gave was truly an 'achishenah' time; Moshiach was ready, and only sin held him back.
The Ba'al HaTanya read 'ha'elef' as heh-elef, since heh and ha are interchangeable, and so found 5775 in the pasuk of the vavim.

The silver of the Yidden beyond 600,000 went to the vavim, whose heads protrude outside the Mishkan's curtains; so they are the Yidden outside the camp, and the vav is missing from the alphabetical kapitlach.
The Yidden outside the camp are connected to the last letters of the Torah that came with the forgetting at Moshe's passing, and Moshe's forgetting the vavim belongs to the same idea.
Hashem's anger at Amalek for attacking Bnei Dan, who were outside the camp, still burns thousands of years later, showing He does not give up on such Yidden.
The closing pei, 'Podeh Hashem nefesh avadav', is the redemption of the missing vav: the Yidden of the end of the Torah return with Moshiach.
Unlike other chachamim, whose dates were for their own days, the Ba'al HaTanya gave a sign close to 200 years after him, for our generation at the end of the Torah.

Following the Imrei Emes, the falls in the house of Yehuda were not from wickedness but by Heaven's design: the king, who includes all his subjects across the generations, had to descend to the lowest depths the nation would ever reach so he could pick them up from there.

The Rav reads the low state of the generation as its strength: just as only earth, the lowest element, creates growth from nothing, the lowest generation is the soil from which the Tzemach David sprouts.

Moav equals forty-nine in gematria and Arvos Moav was the forty-ninth stop in the Midbar, parallel to Malchus shebeMalchus on the last day of Sefirah, so reaching Moav means reaching rock bottom, the point right before the fiftieth, the shofar of Moshiach.

Using the three dimensions of Sefer Yetzirah, the Rav shows Moshiach imprisoned in Moav in place, in soul and in time; the place and soul were already freed when Rus emerged, but the time, Tammuz and Av, still holds him, which is why Bein HaMetzarim equals 'Bas Lot' in gematria.

Ploni Almoni is called a widower of Torah because the chiddush of 'Moavi and not Moavis' was hidden in Rus, and a man's chiddushei Torah are hidden in his zivug; only Boaz, whose zivug she was, could bring it out.
The yud in 'Sdei Moav' stands for Atika, the hidden level beyond understanding, matching why Moshiach must come from so low an origin; once Rus is released the word is written with a heh.
Balak asked to keep Shiva Asar B'Tammuz as his day, supplying korbanos himself so the tamid would cease, yet the Gemara teaches that his very korbanos brought about Moshiach's lineage.

The twelve nesiim of Yishmael are countered by the twelve nesiim of the Mishkan's dedication, so the Chanukah reading of the nesiim makes Chanukah and Kislev a time for nullifying the klipah of Yishmael.
Yishmael's hold on Eretz Yisrael rests on a milah without content, so his claim lasts only while the land is empty of Jews.
The Rav finds 'Yishmael ben Avraham' in the gematria both of 'Hashem melech olam va'ed avdu goyim me'artzo' and of the name Arafat as spelled in Hebrew letters.
The letters of 'barach' each double a value: beis from one to two, chaf from ten to twenty, reish from a hundred to two hundred, so bracha is multiplication in every order.

Six is the number of bracha: Yosef the sixth of the ro'im, the sixth sedra Toldos, its sixth aliyah 'Veyiten lecha' opening with a vav, Yitzchak at sixty, and the lulav shaped like a vav on which the bracha is made.
Just as a talmid at his rebbe's petirah receives a double portion of kedushah, Esav, present at Nimrod's death, received a double portion of tumah; a tzaddik and his adversary die on the same day.

The Rav reads the moment before 'Ani Yosef' as the loss of both Meshichim: Yosef, root of Moshiach ben Yosef, was gone, and Yehuda, seed of Moshiach ben David, was about to become a slave, so the revelation restored both at once.

Galus Mitzrayim, the root of all galuyos, begins with 'Vey, Yidden shreit gevalt', and the final galus under Yishmael ends the same way; the name Yishmael itself guarantees that the cry will be heard.

Serach is counted twice because her good news to Yaakov, who embodied all Klal Yisrael, was a collective besorah like Eliyahu's announcement of Moshiach, so Eliyahu dwelt in her permanently rather than for a moment.
Whichever answer is taken for the seventieth soul, Eliyahu, Yocheved the mother of the redeemer, or Hashem, the one who completes the count of those entering galus is a bearer of geulah.
Asara b'Teves is in one respect graver than Tisha B'Av, since the beginning of the churban contains everything that follows, and Vayigash is read on the Shabbos before it.
Like a coin that lands on heads ten thousand times and still has an even chance of tails, the long wait for Moshiach does not lower the chance that he comes today.
Dates when Moshiach was expected turned into catastrophes because the possibility of redemption threatens the Satan, who comes as accuser and brings up Klal Yisroel's sins.
Ravina and Rav Ashi recorded a date for Moshiach that had already passed precisely as a message to later generations that predictions by tzaddikim may fail, and that this must not shake emunah.
The Rambam's account of Ben Koziva is not history but halacha: even an endorsement by Rabbi Akiva cannot settle who Moshiach is.
The explosion of modern inventions is the Satan's arsenal against Hashem and Moshiach, brought out because he is fighting for his life as the end of the yetzer hara approaches.
Unlike Torah, tefillah always contains lishmah: even a request for a bicycle and a dog is lishmah in the very act of turning to Hashem, which is pure emunah.
Just as at the sea emunah came first and then the song, the geulah from this golus will come through emunah.

Chavakuk's establishing all the mitzvos on one does not mean the others fall away; it means each generation must concentrate its strength on its own avodah, and for the last generations that is emunah.
The term ikvesa d'Meshicha is read literally: the generation before Moshiach is the heel of Adam HaRishon's body, the lowest and darkest limb, which feels nothing and stands only on emunah.
The disappearance of dybbukim is itself a sign of ikvesa d'Meshicha: open glimpses of heaven would make emunah no test, so they were taken away.
The final word of Krias Shema, 'emes', the word the chazzan repeats to complete the 248 limbs, corresponds to the heel, so the last generation's emunah is built into Krias Shema.
Where the Satan invests his greatest effort shows which mitzvah a generation must strengthen: tzitzis in the Divrei Chaim's time, emunah today, attacked through devices brought into the home.

Because the souls of this generation are small and the temptations huge, a small act of restraint is a wonder in Heaven, like the king who is more delighted by a parrot that talks than by a sage who speaks wisdom.
Saying 'if only' is itself the failure of emunah: the businessman's loss was trivial, but blaming his wife denies that Hashem arranged the delay.
David's refusal to take revenge on Shimi made Purim possible through Mordechai and Esther, and since Amalek equals 'safek', doubt, his emunah is what made him the fourth leg of the Divine throne.
The flood of new inventions that tempt people is the Satan's emergency strength before his end, like a candle that flares up just before it goes out.
The Satan concentrates on whoever carries the fate of Klal Yisroel, as with the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur, and so he concentrates on the last generation.
Esav's kiss is the model for modern exile: when the nations can no longer harm Jews with hatred, they harm them with friendliness and the pull of their culture.
The Rav defines emunah as believing even what one does not understand, and leitzanus as dismissing even what one does understand; this is how Pharaoh could shrug off plague after plague.
Although no joke of Pharaoh's appears in the Chumash, the Rav infers he was a joker from the fact that nothing else could have let him withstand the plagues.

Since Malachi was the last prophet, he spoke not only to his own generation but to all generations until Eliyahu, like someone instructing travelers before a long voyage with no word until they reach the shore of Moshiach.

The Rav reads Malachi's 'then those who fear Hashem spoke to one another' as a description of Jews in ikvesa diMeshicha gathering at a mussar shmuess or a Shabbos table with zemiros to strengthen emunah.
He explains Chorev, where the Torah was given, as dry and desolate land, teaching that even when times are dry one must remember Hashem's Torah.
Doubts in emunah are fed by impurity in what one sees: the Rav links the pritzus of the street and failings in kedushah directly to thoughts of doubt and heresy.
In Mitzrayim the fiftieth gate would have been final, but today the power of Torah lets Jews fall even into the fiftieth gate and still hold on.

The Rav compares doubts in emunah to OCD: a person knows the door is locked or his hands are clean and checks anyway; so too a Jew knows the truth, and the doubt is only a 'bug' that must not be indulged.
The Satan fights so hard now precisely because he knows Moshiach is near and his own end is coming, like a man fighting for his life with his last strength.

The words of waiting in davening and in the Shabbos kedushah were instituted for ehrliche Yidden who wait; saying them without waiting would be lying to Hashem, which even an am ha'aretz does not do on Shabbos.
Only one who hoped for Moshiach will be able to say 'hinei Elokeinu zeh kivinu lo' when he comes; one who did not hope will not be able to say it.
The placement of the twelve princes of Yishmael right before 'these are the generations of Yitzchak' hints that their fall opens the way for Moshiach from Yitzchak.
Political events below reflect what happens above: the earthly ruler falls only after his heavenly prince has fallen.
One need not be a Lubavitcher chassid to be on shlichus: every Jew is a shaliach of the Ribono shel Olam.
The present days are historic: when Moshiach comes, volumes will be written about them.
The Rav reads hafrashas challah on erev Shabbos as a reenactment of creation: Hashem kneaded the world and took Adam HaRishon out of it as its challah on the first erev Shabbos.

A person's root in Adam HaRishon fixes what he excels at, not whether he is good: one from the head who does not choose to be a tzaddik becomes a philosopher or scientist, one from the heart a poet or novelist.
Like a fern whose every leaf is a small fern, each generation is a full body of Adam, and the whole chain of generations is again one body from head to heel.
The insensitivity of the heel is by design, so a person can walk on stones; the Rav applies this to our generation's dulled feeling for Yiddishkeit.

Yerushalayim is both the head and the heart of the world: it holds the Lishkas HaGazis and the house of prayer, and the world's constant preoccupation with Eretz Yisroel shows it is the world's heartbeat.
The Purim story, at the end of the Babylonian exile, was itself an ikvesa dimeshicha after the first Churban, parallel to our time after the second.
The Rav reads the Chofetz Chaim's statement as a deliberate withdrawal of the supernatural: dibbukim stopped because open sights would leave no room for the test of emunah.
Tzaddikim today are no smaller; only the permission to show wonders openly was taken from them, so wonders appear rarely, like lightning in the middle of the night.
The Rav applies the sign of a personal test, what is hard yet desired, to a whole generation: collectively, emunah is our test.
Each era has its own target for the Satan: in the Divrei Chaim's time it flooded the market with invalid machine tzitzis, and today it works against emunah itself.
The pollution of air, water and land today is a mirror of the spiritual world, where everything is contaminated as well.
Earlier dates for Moshiach given by gedolim were not mistakes: each was a pekidah, a time especially suited for the geulah had the generation merited it.

An eis ratzon for the geulah that is not merited does not simply pass: the Satan argues that the Jews are unworthy, and the resulting kitrug brings harsh judgment, as the Rav sees in the war that broke out in 1914.

The Rav reads Nitzavim-Vayeilech, one parsha of the Gaon's count, as the current century: Vayeilech's double hester panim is its first half, the Holocaust, and Nitzavim's teshuvah and ingathering is its second half.
Nitzavim, the refuah, precedes Vayeilech, the makah, because Hashem prepares the cure before striking Yisrael, like a surgeon whose prepared bandages show he is a healer and not a murderer.
They are two separate sidros although one parsha because the geulah will be an entirely different order of life, in which the suffering will be remembered like a dream that was not real.
Since the suffering began in the first year of the century, 5700, the Rav hopes this is a sign that the geulah will begin in the first year of its second half, 5750.
The Tree of Knowledge was good: it was a vine whose grapes Adam was meant to press for Kiddush on Friday night, which would have begun an eternal Shabbos; his sin was only that he did not wait.
The Malbim's remark that the maskilim 'know better' than him means only that they may eat on waking, while a Jew must wait: wash, daven and make a brachah first.
Since in loshon hakodesh one root carries both meanings, 'nisayon' as test and 'nes' as raising up reveal each other: the purpose of every test is to lift a person higher.
Avraham's difficulty at the Akeidah was not the deed itself but that he was in katnus: when a person must do something hard, a defense mechanism makes him ask questions.
Not knowing a simple answer is itself part of the test: Avraham, the great sage, did not think of what a child learning Chumash sees, until after the test.
By the Ramban's rule, Avraham's ten tests foreshadow ten tests for the Jewish people, so the last test before Moshiach is the Akeidah's: Hashem seems remote and there are questions without answers.

Dovid HaMelech's recognition, at the moment of Shimi's curse, that Hashem was behind it is what made him the fourth leg of the Divine chariot, and it also brought about that Mordechai, who stood against Haman, would descend from Shimi.
Emunah is the one mitzvah that can stand in for all 613 for souls who have failed again and again, but only if it is complete enough to exclude every 'volt'.
The ecological contamination of recent decades, air, rain, water and food, is a mirror of a spiritual contamination that makes even a blatt Gemara or a kapitel Tehillim harder today than years ago.
The machlokes of great tzaddikim may be l'sheim Shamayim, but when the masses take sides it becomes rechilus and bizayon haTorah, and that is what held back Moshiach then and holds him back now.
In a time of great trials, Torah learned even not for its own sake is precious in Heaven and can tip the scale; the Rav sees in this the different standard by which our generation is judged.
The Rav reads 'prices will soar' as a rise that defies supply and demand: goods are plentiful, the vine gives its fruit, and still the wine is expensive.
Never since the beginning of history was there a government founded on denial of the Creator until the Russian state, which the Rav sees as the fulfillment of 'the kingdom will turn to heresy'.

A dog walks ahead of its master, yet at every corner it turns its head to see which way the master is going; so the leaders of the generation stand in front but take their direction from the crowd behind them.
The shepherd feeds and cares for his flock while the dog only keeps it together; in the heels of Moshiach the leaders will lack the shepherd's role and keep only the dog's.
Like wheat sold in a famine, which no hungry buyer inspects, the mitzvos of the generation before Moshiach are not examined in Heaven, so the time of darkness is a time of great gain.
The Rambam's words 'I await him every day' mean that no day is excluded: one may not make calculations that he will come at one time and not at another.
Adam's sin, the Golden Calf and Shaul's error are one failure, not waiting; David's waiting for the sign began the tikkun, and the avodah of galus is waiting.
Every person is a fragment of Adam haRishon, so each one shares in his sin and must repair his own portion of it.
The disappointments of the era are like birth pangs that end in a stillborn child, a pain Yeshaya already lamented.
Since the first part of the prophecies has been fulfilled exactly, as the Ramban argues about Haazinu, the second part, the geulah, is certain.
The hope for Moshiach is the 'wellspring of yeshuah': by attaching oneself to it, one draws personal yeshuos from it even in galus.
Answering amen is faith in what one has not yet seen, and Hashem keeps every such amen in His treasury.
The mann's whiteness is the point of the rebuke: white is pure chesed, and the mann fed Israel as milk feeds a baby, so complaining about it was complaining against open chesed.
The custom of eating milk in the Nine Days is not merely avoiding meat: white foods draw down the chesed that is hidden in these days, while red meat belongs to sorrow and din.
From every Yom Tov one takes something for the whole year, and from Tisha B'Av, also a moed, one takes the comfort that Hashem is with the Jews in their exile and suffering.
History has its own calendar: the generation of the desert was its Pesach, and ikvesa d'Meshicha is its Tisha B'Av, when every accepted sanctuary is destroyed to make room for the new building.
Avraham's first test had no contradiction to his understanding, but the Akeidah set Hashem's command against Hashem's own promise; its greatness is serving Hashem while the questions remain open.
Tanach places Rus right after Malachi because the building of David's kingdom, like the coming of Moshiach, begins with signs of destruction and chutzpah.
The Rav reads the place of the Mikdash, Rosh Hashana and the king's soul as three parallel 'heads' of place, time and soul, each tied to the first letter of Bereishis that contains the whole Torah.
Only the king could reveal the place of the Mikdash, because its laws are his own portion in the Torah; scholarship alone could not find it from the same verses.
'From the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water' describes not the lowest class of one generation but the last generations, whose avodah in darkness feels like the hardest physical labor.
The later custom that everyone, even children, fasts on erev Rosh Hashana, where the Midrash spoke only of tzaddikim, shows that today's simple Jews are counted as the great ones of the past.
The shofar returns to Hashem the very breath of life He blew into man on Rosh Hashana, so blowing it is crowning Him with one's own soul.
If, as Reb Pinchas says, there is a new Satan every year, then by the principle that good outweighs bad there is also a new yetzer tov every year, so past failures need not decide the coming year.
The darkness at the end of an exile is itself a sign that the salvation is near, because the forces that the tikkun will nullify fight hardest at that moment.
The Rav reads 'bechomer' as kal vachomer and 'bilveinim' as clarifying halacha: the toil that once had to be paid in bricks and mortar can be paid today through toil in learning.
The first and second Batei Mikdash were not eternal because human hands were involved in them, and the same reasoning led the gedolim to reject a redemption brought by nations and armies.
Each churban prepared a later flowering: the bondage of Mitzrayim enabled the Exodus, and the troubles of the second churban prepared Rabbi Akiva's generation, which set down the Oral Torah.

When Yaakov spoke of the end of days, he was looking at the small, leaderless Jews of our generation, wondering how they would hold on, and his advice for them was to gather and speak of the redemption.
The opening of the 'gates of wisdom' expected in 5600 did take place, but the nations seized it, and it became the scientific revolution.

The Rav reads the name 'Toldos' as the theme of the whole sedra: the inner reality of Yaakov's children is not Esav's garments they appear to wear, and their blessing comes from being Avraham's children.
Yishmael's hold on Eretz Yisrael matches his bris: an empty milah earns an empty land, while a Jew's bris is a lifelong guarding of eyes, tongue and bris.
A time ripe for geulah that passes unused does not leave things as they were; because the Satan accuses at such a time, it brings harsher decrees.
The world-wide agreement that Eretz Yisrael belongs to Yishmael may itself be the reversal before the geulah, just as the nations will soon agree to Yaakov's blessings.
From Rashi's calculation the Rav derives that Yaakov's beginning of Torah toil at Shem and Ever is what caused Yishmael's death, so Yishmael's fall comes through Jewish Torah study.
Bachurim, who have no money for tzedakah, can still join in the two things that redeem Israel, since teaching Torah to another is itself chesed.

Rashi's ranking of a tzaddik ben tzaddik applies to an individual's tefillah, but in a tzibur everyone's merits pass through the shaliach tzibur, so a tzaddik ben rasha at the amud adds the merit of drawing near the distant.
The Torah hides the fact of Yaakov's fourteen years in Beis Ever inside the count of Yishmael's years to teach that Yishmael's death came about through Yaakov accepting the yoke of Torah.

The Rav reads Yishmael's control of oil and energy as holding the element of fire, which belongs to Yitzchak; this explains why the Baal HaTurim links Yishmael's fall to the sprouting of Moshiach from Yitzchak's offspring.
A machzor acrostic spells Yitzchak in one column and Rivkah opposite it in words of praise, showing that their prayer 'opposite each other' was praise sung before the salvation.
On the day of passing all of a person's days gather into one, so Eliyahu could give Elisha double what he had only at the moment he was taken.

Rashi's 'thirteen' and the fact that Avraham died when they were fifteen are reconciled: on the day of Avraham's passing Yaakov grew in holiness and Esav, killing Nimrod, grew in tumah, so 'the lads grew' happened that day.

Pharaoh's butler dreamed of working the grapes into wine, a healthy dream of toil, while the baker dreamed of bread growing on his head; the Rav reads the different outcomes as the difference between working for something and wishing for it.

History is a train running between two terminals, creation and the perfected world, on two tracks that seem to lead opposite ways, knowledge and free choice; the question stays unanswered, yet the train keeps running toward its goal.

The ninth of Teves is a fast for a reason not understood, because it continues the darkness that came when the Torah was translated and Jews began to mix culturally with the nations, a darkness in which even Ezra's passing and the loss of true leadership could go unnoticed.

The pairing of Tamar with Potiphar's wife shows two Moshiachs: Moshiach ben Dovid came about through Yehuda's deed, while Potiphar's wife sought Moshiach ben Yosef and Yosef refused, holding that he was obligated only to keep the Torah.
Because the Satan blocks Moshiach, Hashem hides him in the least expected places, like a diamond in garbage, which is why Moshiach's roots pass through Lot, Yehuda and Tamar, and Dovid and Bas Sheva.

Idolatry is rationalization: a person will not admit his weakness and finds an outside justification, and Baal Peor was the idol that made a disgusting act into service of Hashem by its good intention, fitting a sin that began with the intention to bring Moshiach; its gematria equals 'the king Moshiach'.

The pesukim shift from Bnos Moav to Bnos Midian because Bilaam, who knew that Moshiach could come from a union with Moav, sent Midianite women disguised as Moavites, so the tribes' intention could never succeed.

The 'pearl' in Yocheved's birth between the walls is that the root of a thing holds all its strength: the redeemer's mother was born at the very first step of galus, so the redemption is built into the exile itself.
The same Pesach night that fixes the day of yetzias Mitzrayim fixes the day of Tisha b'Av, because Tisha b'Av too must end in geulah.

Serach's news to Yaakov, who embodied all of Klal Yisroel, that Yosef lives was the pattern of Eliyahu announcing Moshiach; therefore Eliyahu joined her, she could not taste death, and she counts as two.
Eliyahu is mentioned on Motzaei Shabbos because the passage from Shabbos, which is like Eretz Yisroel, into the weekdays is a small going-into-galus, and no galus begins without Eliyahu coming along.
Galus is not a bitter fate but the purpose of creation: had redemption been the goal, the souls could have stayed singing by the Kisei HaKavod; they came down to grow in the places of darkness.
A shtiebel is named after the small upper room the Shunamite built for Elisha: small on purpose, so it is roomy for those who seek Hashem and too narrow for a Gechazi who comes for his own gain.
Yaakov's wish to 'dwell in tranquility' was a wish to live the World to Come in this world; because this world cannot hold even a trace of it, the sign turned into reality and the true exile began.
The dreidel, spun on Chanukah while Parshas Vayeshev is read, embodies Rashi's 'gilguleihem': all its turns hide that Moshiach stands at its center, since its letters equal Moshiach.

The eighth king of Edom, Hadar, of whom no death is written, alludes to the 'mehadrin' of Chanukah and to Moshiach; the dark, seemingly unimportant parsha of the kings of Edom hides the whole of Divine providence.
The Greeks broke into the Mikdash; the Chanukah miracle reversed this, sending the lights of the Mikdash out into the weekday, the exile and the public domain.

The Chanukah miracle was not in the oil at all but in time: under the light of Moshiach nature slowed, so the twenty-fifth of Kislev lasted eight days in the Mikdash and the oil burned naturally, allowing a real mitzvah.

A mitzvah works from below to above; in Rabbi Chanina's miracle the light came from above to below, so it was a sign of mercy but not a mitzvah, while Chanukah was a mitzvah and hence 'mitzvas shemonas yemei Chanukah'.

The wicks and oils that may not be lit on Shabbos but may be lit on Chanukah stand for souls that Shabbos cannot kindle, while the light of Chanukah, drawn down by the Chashmonaim's mesirus nefesh, can.
Although the Shechinah never descended below ten tefachim, the Chanukah lamp is placed below ten, because on Chanukah the Shechinah comes down to those lying low who have no strength to rise.
Both parshiyos open with a descent, Yehuda's going down and Yosef's being brought down, hinting that the light of both Mashiachs comes down to the heel, the lowest generation.
Potiphar's wife's intention for Heaven was flawed: Tamar was ready to be burned rather than shame Yehuda, but Potiphar's wife, whose intention was mixed with desire, had Yosef thrown into prison.
Rashi notes that the day was the Egyptians' festival because on that day, the tekufah, Torah is not learned, so Yosef lacked the protection from impure thoughts that, per the Rambam, Torah gives.

The sitra achra always imitates kedushah: as the Jews light up the darkest nights on the 25th of Kislev, the nations darken the 25th of their month with their lights, the opposite of the light revealed on Chanukah.

The Torah hides Yaakov's fourteen years in the yeshivah of Shem and Ever the way someone hides a diamond in a garbage can: inside the count of Yishmael's years, where nobody would look, matching the way Yaakov himself was hidden.
Esav did not pursue Yaakov to Lavan because he reckoned that Lavan, who was Bilam and the essence of impurity, would do a better job of destroying Yaakov than he could.
The seventy souls were the one stage of growth that took place in Eretz Yisrael, because their number stands against the seventy nations, whose borders lie outside the land.

Yaakov's sheep, brought by angels from Lavan's flocks, were the root of the souls of the six hundred thousand who later went down to Egypt; his sticks only made the sheep look as if they came naturally.

Eretz Yisrael is the Shabbos of geography, and galus is the weekday on which one prepares for it: just as only one who toils on Erev Shabbos eats on Shabbos, the nation must be formed in galus to be worthy of the land and of Moshiach.

Vayeitzei comes just before Chanukah, the Yom Tov of weekday clothes, whose menorah is placed on the left side facing the street in the long dark nights, to teach that galus is not only a punishment but the place of Klal Yisrael's growth.

The Rav explains that Moshiach is one comprehensive soul joining Moshe and David, and that until the generation merits its full revelation it can appear in parts, as Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David.
The upheavals before Moshiach are like the cleaning and cooking in a kitchen on erev Shabbos: the noise of preparation for the great Shabbos.
A person looking at a tragedy is like a fly on a great painting that sees only the black spot beneath it; only the great tzaddikim see the whole picture and the old accounts being settled.

Even when a decree is sealed and the tzaddik's counsel seems to fail, a churban that comes while Jews follow the tzaddik is far better, and more are saved, than one that comes through those who rejected him.
The sale of Yosef did not cause the exile, which was already decreed; it only made Yaakov go down to Mitzrayim with honor instead of in chains.
Yisro's question teaches that even the greatest open miracle does not protect from Amalek's coldness; therefore he left Midian to live near Moshe and among the Jews.
Leitzanus is the strongest weapon against truth, because by making something absurd it can dismiss anything without answering it.
The Rav compares the test of the last generation to Avraham's last test, where the Satan's argument made sense and the test was precisely not to listen to it.
The heel of the generations is itself a large area: according to the Satmar Rav it began some 400 years ago, and we stand at its very lowest point.
The talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov broke the normal decline of the generations: they were souls of prophets, sent down for about 150 years to rescue the world.
Because Malachi is the last prophet, his closing words are his message to the last generation on how to cross the sea of galus to the shore of geulah.

Maariv being 'reshus' means it is for special people, and the same ascending order holds for the Shabbos seudos, with shalosh seudos as the greatest; melave malka is a fourth, like chatzos, the tefillah of Dovid HaMelech.
The reversal of purity between land and sea exists so that every species can sing: the pure member in one realm serves as shliach tzibbur for its impure counterpart in the other.
The frog, at home both in the sea and on land, is a mixture of tamei and tahor, so it was the fitting plague for Egyptians who sought to mix good and evil.
The frog's 'Baruch shem' is the song of the sitra achra itself: Hashem wants even the impure realm to praise Him, quietly, through the lower unity.
Tumah is rooted in twoness, which is why Ohalos and Negaim open with 'two'; the frog, being a mixture, needed both one and many, which reconciles Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah.

The frog of Perek Shirah that tells King David its song is finer stands for the Jew of the heel of Moshiach speaking to the generation of the Beis HaMikdash: his weaker song is harder and therefore finer.
The princess who craves the scrapings of the pot is an image for Hashem's preference for the lowly service of the last generation over the finer service of earlier ones.

The fifth week of consolation corresponds to hod, the lowest level, and its haftarah 'for more are the children of the desolate' is the gematria of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the source of strength for the lowest.
The 'forests' that will be stripped bare are the nations and powers that hide Hashem's kingship, the way tall trees in a forest hide the sky and the One who sends all the blessing.

With the Chasam Sofer, the Rav explains that since the Jews already worked at full capacity, the straw decree really took away their Shabbos, and so the shotrim who were beaten rather than force them to work were giving their lives for Shabbos and earned a closer place at Sinai.

Rabbi Moshe of Sambor reads the shift from 'ayal' (masculine) to 'ta'arog' (feminine) as the ayalah who, in her own birth pains, behaves as if she were a male free of them and prays for water for the whole forest.

The flood and Matan Torah are the same flow from Heaven: at the flood the Torah was meant to be given, Moshe's soul was there in Noach, but the generation's sins turned it into a physical, destructive flood.
Noach's failure to pray for his generation made the waters 'mei Noach'; Moshe, the same soul, repaired it when he offered himself with 'mecheini na', and the Zohar reads 'mecheini' as 'mei Noach'.

Bilam's answer to the nations is read as 'Hashem oz l'amo yiten, Hashem yevarech es amo vashalom': the flood this time is Torah, and 'bashalom' contains 'mabul' turned around by the shin of the threefold Torah.

The Rav reads the prohibition of eating new grain until Pesach as reflecting that each year's crop carries a greater light of Hashem's Name, which one is fit to receive only once the festival of redemption has come.

From the Midrash that Scripture says 'yismach' and not 'samach', the Rav learns that Hashem Himself has not yet had complete joy in His world, and therefore no person can attain complete fulfillment before Moshiach either.

Shlomo HaMelech, the fifteenth generation from Avraham like the moon on the fifteenth day, was the one person who fulfilled all his desires, because at the dedication of the Beis HaMikdash he was a sample of Moshiach and the third Beis HaMikdash.
The 'circle dance' of the future means that no one will stand above another and there will be no jealousy; all the tzaddikim will be equal, each pointing to Hashem in the center.
The drum, mere banging on its own, adds life to the other instruments when played with them; so the blows of galus, together with the good times, will be sung to Hashem as kindness.
Pharaoh's calm sleep on the night of the plague of the firstborn was itself arranged by Hashem, so that the plagues of Egypt would become a remedy for the Jews, feeding them with bitachon.

Following Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky, the Rav reads hashpa'ah as related to a slope: influence is something that flows down on its own, so the Jews influence their surroundings even when they think they make no impression.

The laughter of 'Az yimalei s'chok pinu' will be at the nations themselves: they will finally see that the greatness was with the Jews in galus, yet their grasp will remain limited, while the Jews will understand far more.
Galus makes the thirst for Hashem greater than in Temple times, just as a person lost in a desert thirsts more than one who knows water awaits him at home.

Following Rebbe Zusha, both those who serve Hashem with tears and those who serve Him with joy will reap salvation, but the one who sows in tears carries home only the seed, while the one who serves with joy brings whole sheaves.
The faith of the nations in the Creator, crooked as it is, is the planting of the Jews in galus, which is why Israel in galus is called Yizre'el.

Like the sale of Yosef, the sin of the Eitz HaDa'as and the meraglim, the destruction only appears to have been caused by Shlomo; in truth it was all part of Hashem's plan, as will be seen when Moshiach comes.
The first Beis HaMikdash was built in order to be destroyed, so that the Kosel Maaravi would remain as the place of the Shechinah in galus.
The Rav reads 'mishomrim laboker' with Rashi's sense of 'shamar' as waiting for fulfillment: the soul watches for each 'morning' of possible redemption, and when one passes it waits for the next.
Moshe Rabbeinu's first coming, after which the bondage grew harsher, and his second coming that brought the redemption, parallel Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben Dovid.
At times set for a ketz, troubles often come instead of redemption, because the will in heaven to redeem awakens accusation that the Jews are unworthy.
The Tree of Knowledge was meant for squeezing its grapes for Kiddush on Friday night; Adam's sin was eating before Shabbos, so the root failure of the world was not waiting.

The alphabetical verses of Tehillim 34 represent the fixed order of creation and judgment, while the extra verse 'Podeh Hashem nefesh avadav' stands 'outside the brackets' because pedus is beyond that order.
At the Akeidah Hashem wanted Avraham, the attribute of chesed, to bind Yitzchak, the attribute of din, so that din loses its power; this repeats every Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.
Rebbi was punished though the ox was truly created for slaughter, because one who asks asylum must be saved, and so Hashem saves whoever seeks shelter in Him even if guilty.
Balak's parsha is named not for the evil in him but for the hidden thing inside him, the root of Moshiach through Ruth.
Chevron and Shechem, the places of Avraham's milah and of Yosef, are exactly where the enemies fight, because great tumah sits where great holiness lies hidden.
As there is orlah in the body, there is orlah in time: the three weeks are the orlah of the year, and beneath them lies a special brightness.
The two midrashim on Pinchas's covenant fit together: Eliyahu attends the milah of each child and will perform the great milah of the whole world at the geulah.
Tammuz and Av are the months of Reuven and Shimon, fourth and fifth in the degalim; their fall made these months fall, and in the order of tikkun they will be first.
Balak's words 'yoshev mimuli' express his fear that Israel would cut him off as one removes an orlah.
Tammuz and Av correspond to the two eyes, which is why these are the months that call for special guarding of the eyes.

The Mishnah's only law touching Chanukah, the lamp placed below ten tefachim that sets a passing camel's flax on fire, is not incidental: it holds the whole essence of Chanukah, a light that goes down into the public domain.

Chanukah was barely discussed by earlier generations because its light is the hidden light of Moshiach; only generations close to Moshiach, from the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov on, speak of it at length.

Moshiach's ancestry came through hidden, lowly-seeming events so that the Satan, who knows Moshiach will end him, would not notice, like money hidden in the thief's own sack where he will never search.

Tamar waited until she was already burning before sending to Yehudah because the Satan had defeated two earlier chances for Moshiach through Er and Onan, and mesirus nefesh is the one thing he cannot oppose.
Er and Onan, through whom the Satan had blocked Moshiach, came back as Peretz and Zerach, so Tamar's mesirus nefesh repaired the earlier failure.
The Alter Rebbe's arrest was the earthly echo of a heavenly accusation against revealing pnimiyus haTorah, the Torah of Moshiach, which brings Moshiach closer.

The Rav reads the report that the moon helped the attackers on Hoshana Rabbah night together with the shadow seen by moonlight that night and the Ramban on 'sar tzilam', concluding that the moon itself has a share in this war.
The battlefield abroad is only a 'hookup'; the real front of the war is in the batei midrash, where the Jews circle Yericho with the four minim on Hoshana Rabbah and its walls fall.
The three books opened on the Day of Judgment are not lists already written; they are blank, and each Jew registers himself in the book where he chooses to belong.
Writing oneself into the book of tzaddikim without real commitment is like writing a check and not signing it; Hoshana Rabbah and Shemini Atzeres are the signature, the taking of responsibility.

On Shemini Atzeres the Torah does not count the day as it counts the days of Sukkos; the single bull, against the seventy brought for the nations, shows a day when only Hashem and the Jew who is batel to Him exist.
Torah and tefillah strengthen each other: Torah is the mind and tefillah the heart, and both are needed.
Edom, the hardest galus, is the least significant of the kingdoms: like the uncut bird, it need not even be cut; one can step over it.
Edom is a 'robber': its culture, art, literature and scientific progress were all taken from the Jews, and the yetzer hara's strength is likewise stolen from the good part of a person.

The Bris Bein HaBesarim was the birth of the Jewish people, and since a person's destiny depends on the moment of birth, Hashem showed Avraham then the whole future of Klal Yisroel, including the four kingdoms.
Avraham, the root and essence of Klal Yisroel, could have no servitude, since bondage cannot touch the root; a Jew can be enslaved only in his outer part, which relates to the seventy.
The levels of yachid and twelve shevatim have no relation to the nations and so no conflict with them; only at the level of seventy is there a correspondence, and with it competition and galus.

The nations need geographic borders, while the Jews, whose soul is the Torah, remain bound to the inner, heavenly Eretz Yisroel even outside it; so they became seventy souls exactly when they first stepped out of their land into Mitzrayim.

The shevatim correspond to the twelve combinations of Hashem's four-letter Name, which the nations do not relate to, and a Jew reaches this level through his own chiddushei Torah, revealed especially in the month of Shevat.
The gematria of d'tzach adash b'achav is 'Yishmaelim'; since the Yishmaelim began galus Mitzrayim by bringing Yosef down, the wine poured at these simanim draws judgment on them.
A nation that identifies itself with another takes on its din: as the Amalekites who dressed and spoke as Canaanites had the din of Canaan, so the Arabs of Iraq who identify with Bavel are Bavel.
Wine has two powers, drawing kindness to Jews and judgment to the wicked, which is why the Haggadah multiplies the count of the makkos: the more makkos, the more blessing for Jews.

Edom and Yishmael are two kinds of enemy: converts and tannaim came from Edom, but no one converts from Yishmael; correspondingly se'or, inedible, and chametz, edible, are the two kinds of chametz to be burned.
A minhag can be greater than a halachah, because a custom arises from all of Klal Yisrael, which as a whole still has prophecy; hence even reading the Nesiim in Nissan has great power.
The Rav calls Yishmael and Amalek the se'or and chametz of the world, so the pre-Pesach cleaning is part of removing them.
The 'yerach ben yomo' of Masei, a trop found nowhere else, serves the 'karnei parah' of the first Shabbos of Av: the freshness of Nissan serves and repairs the division of Av.
A cow's horn is unfit for a shofar because its layers make it 'many shofars'; the shofar stands for unity and ingathering, while the layered horn mirrors the baseless hatred that caused the exile.

Because Bilaam, Moav and Midian tried to spoil Hashem's ever-fresh love for Israel, measure for measure their impurity is always 'ben yomo', which is why Midian's vessels needed kashering even when not used that day.

Yaakov's gid hanasheh, injured on Tisha B'Av according to sforim, stands for forgotten souls; Shabbos heals it, as Yaakov came 'shalem' to Shechem on Shabbos, which is why Tisha B'Av falling on Shabbos is a sign of healing.
Dinah's captivity in Shechem was not merely a punishment but Hashem's plan: she was born to redeem the spark of Moshiach ben Yosef hidden there, which came out through Osnas.
When Moshiach comes, Jews will long for the exile and even the nations will understand the greatness Israel had in exile.

The custom of learning Sotah in Sefirah is more than a way to keep count: the sotah's barley offering clears suspicion from one woman, and the barley Omer, counted toward Shavuos, clears the suspicion the Egyptians and the nations cast on the purity of all Klal Yisrael.

The order of the generations runs down the body of Adam HaRishon: the generation of the desert, which learned Torah forty years, is the head; David's era of song and tefillah is the heart; and our generation is the heel, so even its leaders are only 'heads of the heel'.

The forty-nine days of Sefirah, the forty-nine levels of Klal Yisrael's descent through the generations, and the forty-nine dafim of Sotah run parallel, so the last daf, with the baraisa of the heels of Moshiach, is our own generation, just before the fiftieth level.
Like Adar, the last month, which turns into Nisan, the first, the lowest generation will be overturned to become the head of all generations together with Moshe and David.

Klal Yisrael began with emunah, with Avraham and with Anochi at Sinai, and it ends with emunah: the closing words of the baraisa, that we can rely only on our Father in Heaven, are the task of the generation before Moshiach.
Even a selfish prayer, such as a boy's request for a dog and a bicycle, is a true tefillah because it rests on believing that Hashem can give, and that belief is emunah.
The name 'seudas reshus' is read as an incomplete phrase: 'reshus' alone lacks a word, and the singing at the meal supplies 'hayachid', turning the public domain into Hashem's private domain.
The lean cows 'stood' because they were stunned, like a person who stops mid-step on seeing Jerusalem: the sitra achra is awed by the power of holiness it swallows.
Like a person who overeats and then vomits not only the excess but everything, the sitra achra will have to spit out all it holds, so that holiness gains from the exile.
The answer to why a calculated ketz passed lies in the passuk of 'Mikeitz' itself, which speaks of Yosef's set time being extended by two years.
Each night's new Chanukah candle is lit in a place in the menorah that was dark the night before, bringing a private domain of holiness into the public domain.
The Rav notes the Rambam's precise wording: attributing troubles to chance is not called wickedness but cruelty, because it brings further troubles on the people.
This week's passuk 'a people heard the voice of G-d speaking from the fire' is read as Hashem speaking to the camp now through its fire, since every passuk applies to every person at every time.

Fire is the one damager that makes no distinction, consuming everything; therefore one who makes havdalah again and again is protected from fire measure for measure, which explains the segulah of relighting the havdalah candle.

The torch for havdalah distinguishes between Jews: the plain Jew sees only gross differences, like kosher shechitah, by a small candle, while the refined Jew needs a torch to see the fine print of the siddur.
Jerusalem was destroyed for keeping to the letter of the law because Jerusalem demands going beyond it; a fire, which does not distinguish, came on those who did not distinguish.
Yerushalayim is yirah and shalem: wherever there is yiras shamayim there is Jerusalem, so each Jewish heart holds a piece of the Mikdash to rebuild.
On the day the enemies ran to defile the sifrei Torah, the bochurim in the camp ran to save the sifrei Torah and tefillin, and the Rav hopes this is remembered favorably in Heaven.
